nodes.title: 📘 README — MiniMax H3 REF2V Turbo + Sage
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3 — REF2V Turbo + Sage

**Read the graph (left → right):**
`A. Configuration` → `B. Models` → `C. LoRA` → `D. Accelerations` → `E. References` → `F. Conditioning` → `G. Sampling` → `H. Decoding` → `I. Export`

### Group switches
- **Bypass**: MODEL/CLIP passes through the group unchanged. Used for C2, D2, and D3.
- **Mute**: the branch does not run. Used for the parallel C3 branch.

### Reading annotations
Each detailed note sits beside one component and explains its settings, purpose, and when to change it. The two notes at the top remain global: they describe the workflow and its prerequisites.

**Validation reference:** RTX A6000 48 GB (Ampere / SM86), ComfyUI 0.31. CUDA and memory settings remain adaptive; do not force a different CUDA stack from this workflow.

nodes.title: 🎚️ BYPASS — D. Accelerations (D1 active / D2·D3 on standby)
🎚️ BYPASS — C2. CLIP LoRA (reserved; empty by default)
🎚️ MUTE — C3. Turbo LoRA branch (ACTIVE — dedicated sampler installed)
📦 Required models and extensions
widgets_values:
## Model files

**`diffusion_models/`**  
`minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`

**`text_encoders/`**  
`qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors`

**`vae/`**  
`minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors`  
`minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors`

**`loras/`**  
`minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema_pruned_comfyui.safetensors`

C3 is enabled by default, so this Turbo LoRA must exist under **this exact filename**, defined in `config.env`.

## Extensions
- ComfyUI core ≥ 0.30
- ComfyUI-KJNodes (Sage Attention patches)
- rgthree-comfy (LoRA, switches, reroutes)
- ComfyUI-VideoHelperSuite (reference video and preview)
- `sageattention` in the ComfyUI environment
- ComfyUI-Spectrum-MiniMax-H3 for D3 only; disabled by default

nodes.title: 📝 Prompt (text + reference tags)
widgets_values:
Cinematic style, nighttime atmosphere. Use <Picture 1> for the character identity and <Picture 2> for the visual style.

CUT 1: ...

nodes.title: 🎬 F. Reference to Video — refs, tags, and size
widgets_values:
## Combining references

This node brings together the prompt, images, video, and audio. Give each reference an explicit role: identity, style, movement, camera, voice, or music.

Tags are numbered **by type** and follow connections: `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`. Audio extracted from a reference video also counts as audio.

### `ref_image_size`
- **`match`** (current): scales images to output size; fast and safest for VRAM.
- **`max`**: preserves more reference detail, but substantially increases time and VRAM at every step. On 48 GB, limit image count and test before a long generation.

Do not change existing wiring just to change a reference role: first change the prompt and loaded files.

nodes.title: 🧠 Diffusion Model — MiniMax H3 Ref2VA (pruned int8 convrot)
🎨 C1. LoRA Stack — style / character (0 active by default)
🎨 C1. LoRA Stack — how to use
widgets_values:
## Style or character LoRAs

**Default:** this node is a passthrough; no LoRA is active and no wiring needs to change.

**Add a LoRA:** click `+ Add Lora`. Each row has its own switch; load several LoRAs and enable them individually for comparison.

This stack affects the diffusion model. Leave CLIP unchanged unless you have a LoRA explicitly compatible with Qwen3-VL/H3 (C2 group).

nodes.title: 🔤 C2. CLIP LoRA — reserved (bypassed by default)
🔤 C2. CLIP reserve
widgets_values:
## LoRA for the text encoder

This node is wired but **bypassed** by default. It is reserved for a future LoRA compatible with the Qwen3-VL/H3 text encoder.

To use it: add the LoRA here, then enable only C2 from the bypasser at the top of the graph. Without a validated CLIP LoRA, leave C2 bypassed.

nodes.title: ⚡ C3. MiniMax H3 Turbo LoRA — official larryvrh node (dedicated, ACTIVE)
⚡ C3. Turbo LoRA — purpose and required file
widgets_values:
## Dedicated Turbo LoRA

This `MiniMaxH3TurboLoRA` node applies the Turbo LoRA to the **MODEL**. It replaces a generic LoRA loader to remain compatible with the downstream `MiniMaxH3TurboSampler`.

**Baseline setting:** strength `1.0`. The v4 LoRA is designed to stay at this value across the 4–8 step range. For fast motion at 4 steps, first move to 6–8 steps: that usually reduces smear / ghosting.

Adjust strength only in response to a specific defect, with a fixed seed: persistent blur or ghosting → raise it slightly (`≈1.05–1.20`); grain or over-sharpening → lower it (`≈0.80–0.95`). Never change strength, scheduler, and steps in the same test.

The displayed filename must be `minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600_ema_pruned_comfyui.safetensors`, which is what the installer downloads to `models/loras/`. C3 is active by default.

nodes.title: ⚙️ D1a. Patch Sage Attention KJ (ACTIVE — combined with Turbo)
💾 D1b. Mem-Eff Sage Attention Patch H3 (ACTIVE — combined with Turbo)
⚙️ D1a. Sage Attention — choosing a mode
widgets_values:
## Patch Sage Attention KJ

This node replaces **MODEL** attention with SageAttention. The `sageattention` library must be installed; this is an experimental patch and must remain easy to disable for A/B testing.

- **`disabled`**: passes the model through unpatched; use it to isolate an issue.
- **`auto`**: delegates implementation choice to SageAttention’s generic function. Useful for compatibility, less explicit for performance comparison.
- **`sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp16_cuda`**: current choice for A6000/Ampere. It calls the explicit CUDA kernel, with Q/K int8 and P/V fp16.
- **`…_triton`**: alternate implementation; try it only in A/B testing if the explicit CUDA kernel fails or regresses.
- **FP8 / SageAttention 3 modes**: do not select by default; they depend strongly on the installed build and GPU architecture.

**PyTorch:** this menu has no “PyTorch mode”. To return to normal ComfyUI/PyTorch/SDPA attention, choose `disabled` or bypass D1.

**`allow_compile`:** keep `false`. At `true`, `torch.compile` may trace into the SageAttention function; it neither compiles nor installs SageAttention. It requires SageAttention ≥ 2.2 and an actual stability test.

nodes.title: 🗄️ D2. Native EasyCache (bypassed by default — test first)
🗄️ D2. EasyCache — A/B test
widgets_values:
## Cache acceleration

EasyCache is **bypassed by default**: it may speed up long clips, but changes the model’s caching strategy. Enable D2 alone, keep D3 bypassed, and compare with identical seed, prompt, duration, and resolution.

The existing values are a node starting point, not a universal recommendation. Keep them for the first test; adjust only after observing a real speed gain without visible loss.

nodes.title: 🌈 D3. Spectrum — experimental
widgets_values:
## Approximate accelerator

Spectrum is **bypassed by default**. It can change the denoising trajectory: even with the same seed, its output can differ from the baseline path.

Do not enable D3 together with D2/EasyCache. Test it alone on a representative short clip, then compare speed, motion consistency, and audio before production use.

nodes.title: → MODEL (after LoRA + accelerations) to G. Sampling
🖼️ E1–E3. Image references
widgets_values:
## Image references

The three loaders are provided for identity, style, and a free reference. They feed `ref_image_0`, `ref_image_1`, and `ref_image_2` on node F.

In the prompt, use `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, and so on in **connection order**, not writing order. Up to 9 images are possible: duplicate a loader and connect it to the next free port on node F.

The actual image cost is controlled by `ref_image_size` on node F; see that node’s note.

nodes.title: 🎥 E4. Video reference — settings and connection
widgets_values:
## Motion and source audio

`reference_motion.mp4` is a placeholder: this node is **muted** and its links to F are removed by default, so the workflow runs without a video.

To use it: select a real video, set the node mode to **Always**, and connect `IMAGE` to `ref_video_0` on node F. Connect `AUDIO` to `ref_video_audio_0` only when you want to reuse the source sound.

**Settings:** `force_rate=24` aligns the reference with output; keep `skip_first_frames=0` unless intentionally trimming; `frame_load_cap=0` loads all frames; `select_every_nth>1` lightens long clips. Prefer a short, representative clip at modest resolution. Duplicate this node for `ref_video_1` and `ref_video_2`.

nodes.title: 🎯 G1. Turbo Sampler — video + audio
widgets_values:
## Sampler dedicated to Turbo LoRA

`MiniMaxH3TurboSampler` supplies noise settings suitable for the model’s two clocks: video and audio. Keep it when C3 (Turbo LoRA) is active.

It automatically adapts to the ComfyUI version: on recent versions with native `ModelSamplingAV` support, it follows the standard path; on older versions, it separates video/audio schedules to avoid distorted audio at low step counts. No manual setting is needed.

The validated Turbo combination here is: Turbo LoRA enabled + this sampler + `simple` scheduler + 4 to 8 steps. Do not replace this node with a generic sampler selector: you would lose this cross-version compatibility.

This node prepares the sampler; actual execution remains in `Sampler Custom Advanced`.

nodes.title: 🎯 MiniMax H3 Turbo Sampler — official larryvrh node (dual video/audio clock)
📈 G2. Scheduler — simple / steps / denoise
widgets_values:
## Noise schedule

The scheduler produces the sigma sequence used by the sampler; it does not choose the sampler itself.

- **`simple`**: current setting and required for the Turbo path.
- **`steps=8`**: a strong compromise. `4` is the minimum; `6–8` is preferable for fast or intense motion.
- **Above 8**: do not use by default. The gain generally stops being visible and over-sharpening artifacts can appear.
- **`denoise=1`**: full generation. A lower value is useful only when deliberately controlling partial denoising with an appropriate latent.

For a reliable test, change one variable at a time. Do not use `LCM` + `Beta` scheduler as a default: that pair has already caused audio issues in this pipeline.

nodes.title: 🎞️ Quick Preview GIF/WEBP (optional — bypassed by default)
🎞️ I3. Quick Preview — WebP/GIF
widgets_values:
## Lightweight preview, not final output

`VHS_VideoCombine` is **bypassed** by default, so it creates no extra file. Enable it only to check framing and motion quickly.

**Current setting:** animated WebP, `MiniMax_H3_preview` prefix, **24 fps** — the same rate as H3 output. The preview therefore reflects the intended duration and motion speed.

Lowering frame rate makes the file lighter, but also plays the same frames more slowly; use that only for a compact shareable preview, not to judge timing.

For production output, always use `CreateVideo → SaveVideo`: this path keeps 24 fps video and synchronized audio muxing.

nodes.title: 🎙️ E5. Audio reference — duration and sample rate
widgets_values:
## Voice or music reference

`LoadAudio` loads the entire file; it has no start or duration controls. If audio is longer than the target video, trim it before importing.

Target 44.1 kHz or 48 kHz. Audio at 32 kHz can introduce artifacts with the H3 audio VAE. In the prompt, describe its role and use `<Audio 1>` according to connection order.

nodes.title: 💾 D1b. Mem-Eff Sage Attention — VRAM
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3 memory patch

This second patch runs **after** the Sage Attention patch on the same MODEL. It aims to reduce H3 attention’s VRAM peak, especially with many references or `ref_image_size=max`.

It has no widget to tune: keep it enabled with D1. To measure its effect, disable it only in a controlled A/B test using the same resolution, duration, seed, and references.
